scope: Fees charged to the person receiving money for goods and services and to business profiles, plus instant transfer. Sending to friends, crypto and the credit card are out of scope.
structure: All Venmo fees are a percentage of the payment or transfer amount (some with a fixed cents add-on), deducted from the amount the recipient receives except the credit-card fee, which the sender pays. Sending money funded by a credit card costs the sender 3.00% (waived when paying a business or charity profile); sends funded by balance, debit card or bank are free. Instant Transfer to an eligible debit card or bank costs 1.75% of the transfer amount, minimum $0.25 and maximum $25, deducted from the transfer; standard transfers are free. Receiving a payment the sender tagged as for goods and services on a personal profile costs the seller 2.99% (no fixed part). Business profiles pay 1.9% + $0.10 of the payment total on every payment of $1.00 or more, or 2.29% + $0.09 for Tap to Pay contactless payments; charity profiles pay 1.9% + $0.10. Crypto buys/sells carry a tiered fee by amount (2.20% / 2.00% / 1.80% / 1.50%) plus a spread built into the exchange rate; PYUSD is fee-free. No rounding rule is published.

notes: The fee tables on venmo.com/resources/our-fees are present in the server HTML but hidden inside collapsed accordions; both plain-HTTP and browser-rendered markdown extractions returned only the section headings, so the values were extracted from the raw HTML.

Tap to Pay fixed component conflict: the fee schedule page and both Tap to Pay FAQs say 2.29% + $0.09, while the 'Business Profile Transaction Fees' help article says 2.29% + $0.10. Two of three sources (including the legal fee disclosure) say $0.09.

Goods-and-services conflict: the fee schedule says 2.99% for payments to a personal profile tagged as a purchase, but the Buying and Selling FAQ example ('$100 ... the recipient would get $98') implies 2% and looks stale (matches the older 1.9% + $0.10 rate).

The $1.00 minimum payment for business/charity profile fees appears only in help articles, not on the fee schedule page; whether payments under $1.00 to a business profile carry any fee is unspecified.
Instant Transfer: the 1.75% fee is deducted from the transfer amount (user receives amount minus fee); minimum $0.25 and maximum $25 apply per transfer.
Credit-card-funded payments to business and charity profiles are exempt from the 3% sender fee (help articles); the fee schedule row states the 3.00% fee without listing that exemption.
Business-profile and purchase-tagged seller fees are not refunded when the seller refunds the buyer.

Crypto: the tiered percentages come from the fee schedule page; help articles only say the fee 'will vary based on the purchase or sale amount', and the PayPal Digital crypto terms say the exchange rate includes a spread and point to fee pages for amounts.
The User Agreement body (which contains the same fee table) did not render (JS-loaded); only its effective date (August 24, 2026) was captured.
No rounding rule is published on any loaded Venmo page.
Venmo's help FAQ shows a personal-profile purchase example of $100 → $98 that contradicts the fee schedule's 2.99% ($97.01); the schedule is used and the FAQ example is not pinned.
summary: Venmo deducts 2.99% from a payment tagged as a purchase on a personal profile, 1.9% + 10¢ on a business profile (2.29% + 9¢ for Tap to Pay), and 1.75% (25¢ to $25) to move money out instantly. Sending funded by a credit card costs the sender 3%.
